text:
sam_prod: Heads-up — ACME Corp private deployment just escalated to security. Customer reports missing audit logs for last 48h and KMS 403s from the runtime. They said this started after a firewall tweak yesterday afternoon. :rotating_light:

maya: Ugh. Any error snippets from their side or our proxy logs?

sam_prod: Customer sent these from their proxy: 
```
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z ERROR tls-proxy: request to https://kms.internal.redwood failed: status=403 body=AccessDenied
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z WARN audit-shipper: unable to upload events: connection reset by peer
```

sam_prod: They also see ephemeral auth succeed for other endpoints but KMS endpoints and our audit shipper to S3/ELK are failing.

elena_cs: Customer is pushing on compliance. They need proof of custody for last week. Can we confirm retention/shipper health?

jorge_sre: Putting on triage. @infra-bot can you pull last 24h of outbound firewall logs for that customer's VPC (vpc-abc123) and NAT gateway metrics?

infra-bot: Requested logs: outbound-fw/vpc-abc123 (2026-03-09..2026-03-10) queued. NAT metrics from nat-agg (1h gran) attached to case.

maya: Likely causes: corporate FW change blocking TLS SNI or ALPN, proxy doing TLS inspection and dropping client certs, or an ACL blocking port 443 to kms endpoints. Also check egress DNS — if DNS is returning internal LB IPs and firewall is default-deny for those ranges.

nilesh_sec: Also consider HSM key policy: if KMS HSM wrapped keys rotated and our runtime lost wrap key access you'd get 403s. But that wouldn't typically break audit shipping. Need to separate KMS auth vs egress.

sam_prod: I repro'd locally by blocking 1.1.1.1 at iptables and got similar audit-shipper errors. Reproducer steps I gave customer: 
```
# simulate blocked egress to kms subnet
sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.240.0.0/16 -j REJECT
curl -v https://kms.internal.redwood/health
# expect 403 or connection reset
```

jorge_sre: Good repro. From infra logs: outbound fw policy was changed at 2026-03-09T15:10 by analyst@example.com — rule DENY egress to 10.240.0.0/16 was added. NAT still up but routes were more restrictive.

nilesh_sec: That rule explains it. Action items: 1) remove DENY for kms subnets or add allow for kms+audit shipper endpoints, 2) verify KMS IAM principal mapping (we'll run list-key-policies), 3) pull audit events backlog and ship with integrity attestation.

maya: I'll draft the minimal firewall exception for customer: allow TCP 443 to kms.*.redwood-internal (10.240.0.0/16) and allow outbound to audit-s3 endpoint 10.241.8.0/24. Also note DNS over HTTPS could hide endpoints, so prefer explicit IP ranges for firewall if they use default-deny.

elena_cs: Customer asked for timeline: can we get initial fix ETA?

jorge_sre: If customer approves immediate rollback, we can flip the rule within 30 min and monitor. Will wait on their OK.

sam_prod: Customer granted permission to rollback. Jorge — proceeding? :+1: 

jorge_sre: Rolling back DENY rule now. Command used (for records): 
```
# cloud-fw cli
cloud-fw rules delete --vpc vpc-abc123 --rule-id deny-egress-kms-20260309
```

infra-bot: Firewall rule deny-egress-kms-20260309 removed (requester: jorge_sre).

sam_prod: After rollback customer reports KMS calls now returning 200 and audit shipper resumed. They still want proof of no data loss for the 48h window.

nilesh_sec: For compliance: collect shipper retry logs, S3 put-object timestamps, and sign a small integrity report. We should also export a hashed index of delivered events and provide an audit timeline to the customer.

maya: I'll prepare a short runbook addendum for Private/VPC customers: checklist for KMS+Audit failures — check egress rules, DNS resolution, TLS inspection, HSM policy, and shipper retries. I'll add sample iptables/curl repro and firewall allow list snippets.

sam_prod: Thanks everyone. Tagging for postmortem: root cause = manual firewall rule added without KMS/audit exception. Follow-ups: runbook update (maya), ensure config guardrail for adding DENY to VPCs with private deployments (nilesh_sec), and customer attestation deliverable (elena_cs).

nilesh_sec: I'll open a follow-up internal ticket to add a pre-commit hook that warns on DENY to redwood-internal subnets.

elena_cs: Customer satisfied with rollback + attestation ETA (EOD). Closing escalation once attestation uploaded. :white_check_mark:
